gaps.sentence: If only I ___ faster — we might still catch the train.
gaps.hint: if only plus could, present inability
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus 'could' expresses a present inability you regret: could run.

gaps.sentence: If the alarm sounds, ___ the building immediately.
gaps.hint: an instruction after if, imperative result
gaps.explanation: Instructions after 'if' keep the present simple in the if-clause and use the imperative as the result: leave.

gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: If you order before midnight, delivery ___ nothing.
gaps.hint: result clause of a first conditional
gaps.explanation: The result of a real future condition takes 'will': will cost.

gaps.sentence: As long as you ___ the rules, you will have no problems here.
gaps.hint: as long as states the condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: follow.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me, I would have helped you move house.
gaps.hint: a missed request in the past
gaps.explanation: An unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had asked.

gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: As long as nobody ___, we will finish before lunch.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a present verb
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' clauses take the present simple: objects.
